sentences.text:
Applicant has filed this third bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 on behalf of the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.41/2022 registered at P.S. Crime Branch, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420,
409, 120-B and 34 of IPC.
2. His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court.

3. Applicant has filed this third application for grant of bail on the ground that after rejecting his earlier bail application, complainant Devendra (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and he has turned hostile.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.

Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Shivam Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160521848/
1

entities.text: Shivam Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

5. Learned counsel for objector also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that applicant's first bail application was dismissed on merit by this Court vide order dated 09.12.2022 passed in MCRC No.55275/2022 after considering all the facts and circumstances of the case.

Hence, he does not deserve for bail.
6.
Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.

7. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that applicant's earlier bail application was dismissed on merit and after that, complainant Devendra (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and he has supported the case of the prosecution and has deposed against the present applicant, therefore, the case of the prosecution became more stronger than earlier.
There is no material change in which the applicant can be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, the present bail application preferred under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is dismissed.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Shivam Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160521848/
